decisionUnit.cohort: Enterprise administrators and developers reviewing exact source-bound AI tooling policy; release maintainers supplying verifiable Core artifacts.
decisionUnit.outcome: Author reviewable offline policy intent across source providers while preserving exact evidence, target constraints and distinct qualification/publication/acceptance/promotion authority.
includedChanges: Schema-v3 normalized Workbench authoring with Core0.6 minimum feature floor.
Source-provider separation and exact saved ECC runtime data; canonical upstream evidence binding.
Pinned Matt Pocock and Ponytail catalog additions, readable scan metadata and source browsing.
Requested AIH MCP intent, target intersection and withheld unverified legacy authority.
Scanner publication consumption and bounded analyzer/toolchain security updates.
Candidate-first enterprise delivery and exact public installed acceptance.
Documented npm user-owned prefix recovery for global installation permission failures.
Explicit reviewed Core 0.5.x and 0.6.x built-in capability compatibility, preserving enterprise approval and refusal of unreviewed minor lines.
Fix-forward release packet staging preserves exact enterprise-manifest and qualification-evidence paths after the failed immutable Core 0.6.0 qualification.
Exact Core 0.6.1 first-party evidence intake from the published sequence4 Catalog, with all prior provider evidence and Scanner findings preserved.
Fresh hosted public npm832, managed and supported npm848 acceptance with encrypted raw evidence retention; actual execution remains required before promotion.
decisionUnit.adoptionRationale: Optional adoption for organizations needing the new governed Workbench authoring model. Evaluate the exact candidate with existing policy and approved source pins; this release does not require a forced migration.
prerequisites: Successful final merged-main preflight, exact candidate verification and protected qualification recorded on release tracker #987.
Core version floor and compatible exact Scanner/Catalog versions; preserved prior policies and custody.
Existing Catalog owner signature, approved public seq4 receipt set and exact attestation before supported npm journey.
Exact npm Trusted Publisher tuple and protected environment approval; no token fallback.
Public installed acceptance with zero skipped legs and actual released-byte npm/managed journeys before released-feature claims.
decisionUnit.rollout: Evaluate the qualified exact candidate under next in disposable roots. Review policy diffs and requested/effective state with a small administrator cohort. Expand only after exact public acceptance and a separately authorized stable promotion; keep existing approved pins until organizational approval.
decisionUnit.rollback: Stop rollout, retain evidence and revoke newly owned effects where appropriate. Restore saved compatible policy/approved package pins; inspect custody before downgrade. Owner may restore prior accepted latest tag; never move immutable git tags or rebuild an existing version.
decisionUnit.supportImpact: Schema-v3 consumers require Core 0.6 or a compatible successor. Administrators must distinguish requested intent, conditional local acceptance and verified public authority. The final public OS/Node matrix and required npm/managed journeys must pass before stable promotion.
decisionUnit.accountableOwner: samartomar (Core release maintainer; release tracker #987 assignee)

knownIssues: Immutable Core 0.6.0 failed receipt sealing before publication. Core 0.6.1 must independently qualify and publish its own exact bytes; prior package checks and installed tests do not supply a successful qualification receipt.

Catalog sequence4 publication is verified at exact source98d95263aa0901504c9d480628f6c06c4a1fe453. Actual public Core 0.6.1 supported npm and managed journeys remain required before completing release tracker #987.

Retained npm and managed journeys on Core 0.5 development bytes are separate evidence. Required final Core 0.6 public registry journeys and installed OS/Node acceptance must pass before stable promotion.

Core 0.6 includes 524 Workbench records. Final candidate checks must prove complete evidence coverage and live publication-material equivalence on its exact bytes; coverage readiness alone is not scan or release acceptance.
The native-only picocolors 1.1.1 scan remains missing/warn with nine explicitly scoped coverage gaps. Conditional local acceptance does not make it a successful scan or blanket waiver.
The broader #940 external-pin qualification campaign and historical Core 0.5 acceptance #972 remain separately open; this release does not claim their completion.
The total 60-second Workbench runtime target remains follow-up #986. Functional behavior, per-test deadlines, the pure ten-second budget, coverage and security remain required.
